lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
Date of birth: 3 Mar 1997 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Owned the monthly patient survey and the reporting dashboard the care teams used.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; my findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Wrote the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
- Improved dispute-form completion by 40% by splitting the form into three short steps with saved progress.
- Ran 18 moderated usability sessions a quarter from a recruiting panel of 400 customers, so every major release was tested with real account holders before launch.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Raised the onboarding flow's System Usability Scale score from 68 to 104 across two rounds of moderated testing with 20 customers.
- Validated the redesigned app navigation's findability with an open card sort of 30 customers before it shipped.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Cut median route-finding time from 90 to 60 seconds, a 50% improvement, by adding audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
- Published the design files and test protocol openly, and the city's transit agency invited the project to its spring accessibility review.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Conducted user interviews and created wireframes for a free clinic's online booking flow.
- Recruited 10 clinic patients and ran two rounds of hallway testing, fixing the six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA)
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interviews, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: Date of birth and nationality are personal details the résumé should not include.
items.because: They direct attention to personal information rather than qualifications.

items.says: Move EXPERIENCE above EDUCATION.
items.because: Several years of relevant work now demonstrate fit better than the earlier degree.

items.says: List experience newest-first, with Pinegrove Financial above Northwind Health.
items.because: Readers may not see the latest role and seniority as quickly.

items.says: The survey-and-dashboard bullet does not show what the work changed for care teams or patients.
items.because: Without a decision or action it enabled, the line reads as responsibility rather than evidence of impact.

items.says: “Owned” names responsibility without showing how the survey was run or the dashboard maintained.
Move the reminder-research bullet ahead of the survey-and-dashboard bullet.
items.because: Its concrete change and reduction in missed appointments should lead the entry.

items.says: “My findings” uses a first-person pronoun in a résumé bullet.
The 30% reduction in support calls lacks a measurement period or comparison window.
items.because: Readers cannot tell when calls were counted or what period the reduction compares.

items.says: “About joining a video visit” is wordier than necessary.
“In the quarter after launch” expresses the timing less efficiently than “post-launch.”
“Improved dispute-form completion by 40%” does not distinguish a relative increase from a percentage-point increase.
items.because: Those describe different amounts of change.

items.says: The coverage clause says releases were tested but not what the testing changed or achieved.
items.because: Readers can see that research happened regularly, but not what it contributed to the product or business.

items.says: The explanation of the sessions’ purpose is longer than necessary.
“Synthesizing” uses present-participle form for a completed role described in the past tense.
items.because: The tense shift can make the work sound ongoing despite the completed role dates and past-tense result.

items.says: The 23% reduction in repeat support calls is buried after a long list of inputs and methods.
items.because: A scanning reader reaches the methods before the strongest evidence of impact.

items.says: A standard System Usability Scale score cannot be 104.
An open card sort does not validate findability in a particular navigation.
items.because: It reveals how participants group and label content, not whether they can find items in a designed navigation.

items.says: The line does not say what the card sort revealed or changed.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether the research uncovered a problem, confirmed a decision, or affected the shipped design.

items.says: “Before it shipped” is unnecessary timing detail.
“On timed route-finding tasks” is wordy and indirect.
The change from 90 to 60 seconds is a 33.3% reduction, not a 50% improvement.
items.because: The decrease is 30 seconds out of the original 90 seconds.

items.says: The percentage repeats the time reduction without adding information.
items.because: The 90-to-60-second figures already show that route-finding time fell.

items.says: The agency invitation, the strongest outcome, follows a long publication clause.
items.because: Readers encounter the publication detail before the more distinctive invitation.

items.says: “Openly” is redundant.
items.because: “Published” already conveys that the materials were made public.

items.says: The line does not say what the agency review covered or what followed from the invitation.
The line names interviews and wireframes but not the redesign’s outcome or evidence.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether booking became easier or more successful.

items.says: “Hallway testing” is team-specific jargon that may be unclear outside the field.
“The six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking” is wordy.
